extracted.intended_audience: agency officials, rulemaking practitioners, legal scholars, and public commenters/advocates
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and recommendations to improve transparency and public participation in federal rulemaking, aimed at agencies and stakeholders involved in notice-and-comment processes. Emphasizes timing, outreach, document accessibility, administrative-record quality, and e-rulemaking systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek citizen comment earlier (pre-NPRM engagement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should seek citizen comment earlier in the rulemaking process, i.e., before issuance of a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (pre-NPRM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Task Force emphasizes that engaging EARLY (pre-NPRM) is more influential than late engagement. Early outreach can surface issues before positions harden, shape agency thinking, and improve the quality of later formal comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reach out to all affected groups in an evenhanded manner
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should proactively reach out to all affected groups and stakeholders in an impartial and evenhanded way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diverse stakeholder participation matters for the legitimacy of rulemaking. Outreach should be designed to include underrepresented or less-resourced constituencies so that comment pools are not dominated by a narrow set of interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve the quality and accessibility of regulatory documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory documents should be easier to access and written in ways that improve public understanding and engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide plain-language summaries of proposed rules and improve usability of documents so that the public can meaningfully review and comment. Accessibility includes both format/usability and clarity of exposition (plain language).

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthen the administrative record and completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the administrative record for rulemakings is complete and well-developed to support agency decisions and later review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments that help build out the administrative record support later legal challenges; agencies should adopt practices to maintain a robust record. Administrative record completeness is also listed as a strategic management priority requiring sustained attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve e-rulemaking system (Regulations.gov) usability and data quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhance Regulations.gov and related e-rulemaking infrastructure focusing on access, usability, data quality, and timeliness of data entry into the Federal Docket Management System.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targeted recommendations include (i) ease of access and usability of Regulations.gov, (ii) quality of data being uploaded, and (iii) timeliness of agency data entry into the Federal Docket Management System. Better e-rulemaking systems increase participation and the practical usefulness of submitted comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide plain-language summaries of proposed rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should provide plain-language summaries alongside technical rule materials to make proposals understandable to lay audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plain language matters both from agency to public and from public to agency. Summaries lower barriers to participation and improve the quality of public input by making the substantive issues clearer to nonexperts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple notification channels beyond the Federal Register
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ multiple outreach and notification channels in addition to publication in the Federal Register to inform potentially affected parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relying solely on the Federal Register limits notice. Agencies should use alternative and supplementary channels to increase reach and ensure that diverse stakeholders learn of proposed rules in time to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop and track public participation metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should create and monitor metrics to assess public participation over time as part of strategic management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public participation metrics are a strategic recommendation requiring sustained attention; such metrics can help agencies evaluate whether outreach and e-rulemaking improvements are effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve comment response practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should adopt better practices for responding to public comments to ensure meaningful consideration and a clear administrative record of how input was used or rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengthening comment response practices contributes to administrative-record quality and transparency. Clear responses help stakeholders understand agency reasoning and improve legitimacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase transparency of OIRA review
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhance the openness of Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs (OIRA) review processes to improve overall rulemaking transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OIRA review transparency is identified as a strategic management priority; making review processes and rationales more visible can improve accountability and public trust in regulatory outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit comments that substantively engage with agency reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Public comments should engage substantively with the agency's stated reasoning, evidence, and legal/technical bases for a proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive engagement with agency reasoning is critical—comments that merely express support or opposition without engaging the agency's analysis are less influential. Well-reasoned, evidence-based comments better build the administrative record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribute to the administrative record to support potential challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments should aim to build out factual and legal information in the administrative record that could be used if the rule is later challenged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Task Force notes that comments which build the administrative record strengthen future judicial or administrative challenges; commenters should provide evidence, citations, and reasoned argumentation to do so.
